lyrics:
No home to drive to
Just the lights up ahead

I drove until I lost the road
no house left with my name on the door
Some field still lit up like it glowed
a carnival I'd never seen before

The God I built looked just like him —
my father's face, my father's frown
A ledger kept in perfect trim
and me already marked far down
No mercy written in the fine —
just interest owed on every line

In the image of the hand I knew
I built You strict. I built You cold
Every rule I couldn't get through
just the family creed, grown old

Past the ring toss, past the noise
a single bulb, a folding chair
Some new self help hustle
and a woman waiting there

In the image of the hand I knew
I built You strict. I built You cold
Every rule I couldn't get through
just the family creed, grown old

When you kloze your eyes and look at yourself, what do you see
It's not pretty
When I kloze mine, I see something more: God, in the image of you

I didn't answer. Didn't speak
The lights went out row by row
I wasn't sure what I should seek —
or if I even wanted to know

[Intro - hollow, drifting]
No home to drive to.
Just the lights up ahead.

[Verse 1 - flat, bottomed out]
I drove until I lost the road,
no house left with my name on the door.
Some field still lit up like it glowed,
a carnival I'd never seen before.

[Verse 2 - cold, remembering]
The God I built looked just like him —
my father's face, my father's frown.
A ledger kept in perfect trim,
and me already marked far down.
No mercy written in the fine —
just interest owed on every line.

[Chorus - hard, resigned]
In the image of the hand I knew,
I built You strict. I built You cold.
Every rule I couldn't get through,
just the family creed, grown old.

[Interlude - carnival calliope, unsettled]

[Verse 3 - quiet, arriving]
Past the ring toss, past the noise,
a single bulb, a folding chair.
Some new self help hustle
and a woman waiting there.

[Chorus - hard, resigned]
In the image of the hand I knew,
I built You strict. I built You cold.
Every rule I couldn't get through,
just the family creed, grown old.
[Dialogue - start]
[Geneva - warm, gentle - female vocal]
When you kloze your eyes and look at yourself, what do you see?
[Him - flat, spent - male vocal]
It's not pretty.
[Geneva - warm, certain -  - female vocal]
When I kloze mine, I see something more: God, in the image of you.
[Dialogue - end]
[Outro - quiet, unresolved - male vocal]
I didn't answer. Didn't speak.
The lights went out row by row.
I wasn't sure what I should seek —
or if I even wanted to know.

[End]
style: Slowcore/ambient folk, unhurried 52 BPM minor-mode pulse; near-silent fingerpicked nylon guitar, felt-piano single notes, bowed upright bass, distant harmonium drone, brushed snare and rim clicks, brief unsettled carnival calliope interlude; dry close-mic tape-hissed mix with sparse dark reverb; nearly whispered male baritone and warm female alto in restrained dialogue, English vocals

impression.text: This track establishes a sparse and deeply melancholic texture, driven by intimate acoustic guitar fingerpicking and breathy male vocals. The overall energy remains hushed and contemplative throughout the entire piece, creating an emotionally vulnerable feel. Production-wise, the mix is incredibly spacious with a low density that allows the delicate vocal layers and subtle ambient swells to sit seamlessly around the core acoustic arrangement. A highly distinctive moment occurs late in the song when a haunting spoken-word dialogue between a man and a woman emerges, cementing the cinematic and deeply reflective atmosphere of the track.

review.review_text: The theology here is the whole game: "The God I built looked just like him, my father's face, my father's frown," a man discovering he inherited a deity along with a ledger and a grudge. Rose keeps it starved, close-miced fingerpicking in what sounds like a minor key, a baritone that never rises above the volume of thinking out loud, and a spooked little carnival interlude that arrives right when the road runs out. The masterstroke is the late dialogue, Geneva flipping his self-loathing on its head with "I see something more: God, in the image of you," and Rose refusing to answer: "I didn't answer. Didn't speak." That withheld ending is braver than resolution, cousin to the patient silences of 'You Don't Say,' and it lands cleanly.
